surfaces.part: backrest/seat cushion run (stepped teal band, lit top row then darkening gradient)

answer.evidence: The chair is drawn as a side profile. The teal body steps diagonally down from the headrest on the left to the leg rest on the right. Each segment has a 1-row light top highlight (rows 11, 13, 15) that grades into darker teal below. That reads as cylindrical shading, not a horizontal seat plane. The silhouette widths (rows 10-19 vary 12-27) follow the diagonal, with no widen-then-narrow ellipse and no front-edge line plus eave shadow. The pole (rows 18-25, width 6) and base (rows 24-28) show only a 1-row top highlight at row 25. No sitting surface is seen from above, so the seat has at most a 1-2 row rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small teal chair with a grey lamp arm. It uses only 12 distinct colours across all materials, against 38-40 for the well and the stall, so each material (teal body, grey metal) gets about 3 lightness steps, where Beodeul uses 5-6. The outline is tinted dark blue-grey rather than neutral (0% near-neutral dark edges), so it reads as a dark material tone and not a black sticker line. The measured facts are acceptable: 11 visible tones per tile (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20) and 0% near-flat coverage. By eye, though, the large teal surfaces are smooth with few texture dots, grain or per-part highlights, and the form is simple and a little thin next to the stall and well. The shading is shallow and the piece would look flatter than the references if placed beside them, so it fails.

This matches the 'side elevation chair' red reference, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours across the whole piece. Its teal and grey-blue ramps are therefore shallow, about 3 steps each (highlight, mid, dark), against the 5-6 steps of the Beodeul references. The outline is a tinted dark blue-grey (0% near-neutral edge pixels), not a black sticker line, which is a point in its favour. The tile facts look acceptable: 11 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, and 0% near-flat coverage.
